You said:
what's the purpose of variable list in useEffect
ChatGPT said:

In React, the "variable list" you pass as the second argument to useEffect is called the dependency array. Its purpose is to tell React when to run (or re-run) your effect.

Here’s how it works:

1. No dependency array (useEffect(() => {...}))

  • The effect runs after every render.

  • Can easily cause performance issues or infinite loops if you update state inside.

2. Empty dependency array (useEffect(() => {...}, []))

  • The effect runs only once, after the component mounts.

  • Commonly used for things like fetching initial data, subscribing to events, or initializing.

3. Dependency array with variables (useEffect(() => {...}, [a, b]))

  • The effect runs:

    • After the first render, and

    • Whenever any of the listed variables (a or b) change.

  • This is how you “react” to state or prop changes.

Example:

jsx
useEffect(() => {
  console.log("User ID changed, fetching data...");
  fetch(`/api/user/${userId}`);
}, [userId]);

Here, the effect only re-runs when userId changes.

4. Why it matters

  • Without the dependency array, you risk unnecessary or infinite re-renders.

  • With it, React optimizes when to run effects.

  • It makes your component predictable and efficient.

👉 In short:
The dependency array (“variable list”) tells React what values your effect depends on so it knows exactly when to run it again.

Would you like me to also explain what happens if you leave out a variable that your effect uses? That’s a common pitfall with useEffect.

ChatGPT said:

Short answer: don’t put cards there. Your effect doesn’t use the list value at all—it uses cardsHandlers and isDraggingOverDivider (plus the two setters, which are stable).

Use this:

tsx
useEffect(() => {
  return useGlobalEventListeners(
    cardsHandlers,
    isDraggingOverDivider,
    setIsDraggingOver,
    setIsDraggingOverDivider
  );
}, [cardsHandlers, isDraggingOverDivider]); // ✅

Why:

  • The handlers you attach close over isDraggingOverDivider and cardsHandlers. If either changes, you want new listeners with fresh closures.

  • setIsDraggingOver and setIsDraggingOverDivider are React state setters—they’re stable and don’t need to be in the deps.

  • Including cards would cause unnecessary unsubscribe/subscribe cycles on every list change even though the listeners never read cards.

(Optional) Fewer re-subscribes: use a ref

If you want to avoid reattaching listeners whenever isDraggingOverDivider changes, keep the latest value in a ref and subscribe once:

tsx
const dividerRef = useRef(isDraggingOverDivider);
useEffect(() => {
  dividerRef.current = isDraggingOverDivider;
}, [isDraggingOverDivider]);

useEffect(() => {
  const cleanup = useGlobalEventListeners(
    cardsHandlers,
    /* read from ref inside the handlers instead of this arg */
    dividerRef.current,
    setIsDraggingOver,
    setIsDraggingOverDivider
  );
  return cleanup;
}, [cardsHandlers]); // or [] if cardsHandlers is stable in your lib

In that version, your event handlers should read dividerRef.current instead of the prop so you can keep the dependency list minimal and avoid frequent re-subscribes.
